name: Orokk Omosh
summary: In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh seeks apprentices for his family's smithing craft. With no children to inherit it, he hopes worthy Horde smiths will carry the Omosh armorcraft secrets onward.

sections.title: A Lineage at Its End
sections.body: Orokk Omosh is the last smith of his line in the Valley of Honor. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. So he sets demanding trials of metalwork for capable Horde blacksmiths. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft.

sections.title: The Spirit of the Forge
sections.body: Among the artisans, Orokk is known for his boisterous delight in true mastery. When smiths complete his craftsmanship trials, he often performs the Omosh Dance of Joy. His jubilant celebration of traditional smithing echoes through Orgrimmar's halls.

faq.answer: Orokk Omosh is an aging orc blacksmith in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. The last smith of the Omosh line, he seeks worthy Horde apprentices to preserve his family's craft.

faq.q: Where can Orokk Omosh be found?
faq.answer: You can find Orokk Omosh beside the smithing forges and anvils in Orgrimmar's northeastern Valley of Honor.

faq.q: Why is Orokk Omosh teaching outsiders his family secrets?
faq.answer: Orokk has no children to inherit his family's craft. He teaches skilled Horde blacksmiths who prove themselves in his trials, so the Omosh techniques do not die with him.

faq.q: What is the 'Omosh Dance of Joy'?
faq.answer: The Omosh Dance of Joy is a jubilant jig Orokk performs when an artisan proves their worth and masters his line's smithing techniques. It is his spirited tribute to the craft.

angles.text: As a Horde blacksmith, you can learn from Orokk Omosh and help preserve his family's ancestral craft.
As a member of the Horde, you can help keep traditional orcish plate and mail techniques available to the warriors defending the fledgling Horde.
